claim: Expert parallelism's communication volume is a per-layer token dispatch of Seq x TopK per direction, and the Pangu system reduces the inter-node share of that to Seq x (EP-1) by converting inter-node All-to-All into an inter-node AllGather followed by an intra-node All-to-All.
stance_target: the repo's claim that EP does two all-to-alls per MoE layer and that the volume is set by tokens x top-k
scope_conditions: 718B MoE, 256 experts, topk=8, EP over Ascend 910B nodes; Table 4 communication-volume comparison
quoted_support: Table 4: Comparison of communication volumes. Hierarchical EP All-to-All Communication converts inter-node All-to-All to intra-node All-to-All. Total communication volumes are reduced. ... Inter-node Seq x TP x EP (Allgather) | Seq x TopK (All-to-All) | Seq x (EP-1) (Allgather); Intra-node - | - | Seq x TopK (All-to-All).

claim: Traditional All-to-All in expert parallelism does not distinguish intra-node from inter-node traffic, which produces suboptimal bandwidth utilization and inflated communication overhead — the reason they restructure dispatch hierarchically.
stance_target: the repo's claim that EP's all-to-all is the dominant communication cost on a fabric without a fast intra-node domain
scope_conditions: Ascend 910B clusters where EP size exceeds the NPUs in one node
quoted_support: Traditional All-to-All communication in expert parallelism does not distinguish intra-node and inter-node traffic [51], leading to suboptimal bandwidth utilization and increased communication overhead.

claim: Overlapping EP all-to-all with finer-grained compute (Adaptive Pipe Overlap) is worth +28.6% MFU on its own over the baseline — i.e. the communication they could not remove had to be hidden behind compute to stop it binding.
stance_target: the claim that on a slow fabric EP cost can only be hidden by overlap, and that the hiding is worth tens of percent of throughput
scope_conditions: 718B MoE training on 6K Ascend NPUs; Table 5 cumulative MFU attribution
quoted_support: Strategy MFU increase: baseline 1; + fine-grained recompute and swap 15.8%; + adaptive pipe overlap 28.6%; + host optimization 49.2%; + fused operators 58.7%.

claim: Training a 718B MoE on 6K Ascend NPUs reaches 30.0% MFU and 1.46M tokens/s, versus 18.9% MFU and 0.61M tokens/s for the 4K-NPU baseline — a 2.4x throughput gain from the combined parallelism and overlap work.
stance_target: what a well-tuned EP stack buys on a dedicated fabric, as the ceiling against which a Gen2 x4 box should be judged
scope_conditions: Pangu Ultra MoE 718B, 6K Ascend 910B NPUs, TP(8) x EP(4) partitioning
quoted_support: we achieve an MFU of 30.0% and Tokens Per Second (TPS) of 1.46M on 6K Ascend NPUs, compared to the baseline MFU of 18.9% and TPS of 0.61M on 4K Ascend NPUs.

claim: An excessively large EP degree introduces large communication overhead and causes performance degradation, so the EP degree is chosen by joint optimization against memory usage and communication cost rather than maximized.
stance_target: the repo's claim that EP is not a free lever and that EP degree must be traded against fabric bandwidth
scope_conditions: MoE architecture search for Ascend NPUs; EP degree selection
quoted_support: EP is also an effective tool for reducing memory access and memory usage per NPU, however, an excessively large EP value introduces large communication overhead, causing performance degradations.

claim: Applying large tensor parallelism to granular experts (2048 intermediate size) shrinks the per-matmul tensor size enough to lose MatMul efficiency — TP and fine-grained MoE experts interact badly even on a fast fabric.
stance_target: the repo's claim that tensor parallelism is a poor fit for MoE on this box, independent of the link
scope_conditions: Ascend NPUs, 256 experts with 2048 intermediate size, TP(8) x EP(4)
quoted_support: Besides, applying large TP on granular experts (2048 intermediate size) will reduce the tensor size, potentially leading to low MatMul efficiency.

claim: The MoE block design was fixed by pilot runs on a 20B-total / 1.6B-active model (256 experts, topk=8 including a shared expert) plus a throughput simulator, rather than by full-scale trials — a reduced-scale pilot plus simulation is the accepted method for choosing MoE configs.
stance_target: the repo's plan to pick MoE configs from ~1B-scale pilots before committing GPU-days
scope_conditions: Pangu Ultra MoE architecture search, Section 2.1
quoted_support: This model consists of 256 total experts, activates topk=8 experts per token (including a default shared expert unless specified), and contains approximately 20B total parameters, with 1.6B activated per token.

claim: The paper's communication analysis assumes a two-tier fabric (fast intra-node HCCS, slower inter-node network) and spends its effort moving traffic from the slow tier to the fast one; a 5-GPU box has no fast tier at all, so the hierarchical trick has nothing to exploit.
stance_target: whether the hierarchical-EP optimization transfers to a flat Gen2 x4 fabric
scope_conditions: Ascend 910B node topology; EP size exceeding NPUs per node
quoted_support: Experts are distributed across multiple nodes when the EP size exceeds the number of NPUs in a single node, leading to inter-node communication with much lower bandwidth than intra-node bandwidth. To address this, we propose a Hierarchical Expert-Parallel Communication Mechanism which strategically restructures the communication flow to prioritize intra-node transfers in two phases.
